content.text: I read every input file, the full draft, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, and traced each element back to the inventor's own words.

input.summary:
Full source-fidelity preflight completed against input/disclosure.md and input/conversation.md as the sole affirmative authority (conversation.md is a truncated duplicate of the disclosure and adds nothing), with input/brief.md used only for formalities (title, applicant/inventor, no priority claim, no federal support, preserved terminology).

Claims: all 22 claims were traced limitation by limitation. Claim 1 (rail with flat lower face, upper face, first/second ends, first/second longitudinal sides, slot through rail, distance marks alongside the slot; fence secured by two screws in two corresponding mounting holes, perpendicular, downwardly projecting portion, reversible between first and second longitudinal sides with the marked face still outward; two separately seated carriages each with anti-rotation key in the slot, cylindrical drill bushing whose bore passes completely through and registers with the slot, clamp knob whose threaded shank passes through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail; parallel bores perpendicular to the lower face; two pointers aligned with the bore axes and readable against the marks) maps sentence for sentence onto the disclosure. Dependent claims 2 (separate, uncoupled, independently clamped), 3 (difference of readings = center-to-center spacing), 4-6 (midpoint transverse center index, shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with it, alignable with a marked centerline), 7 (removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces, setback changed by its thickness, separation unchanged), 8 (marks read in the same direction in both fence orientations, from "the same marked upper face be used ... from either an upper edge or a lower edge"), 9-10 (hardened-metal replaceable wear-part bushings; rigid polymer or metal for rail, fence, carriage bodies, shoes, pointers, knobs), 11-12 (no motor/battery/electronic sensor/network; shoe below and bearing on the lower face), independent claim 13 and 14-17, and method claims 18-22 (loosen, slide to a difference equal to the selected spacing and equal distances about the center index, tighten, place, press fence or spacer against the edge, align notch and index with the centerline, drill both bushings, lift away with nothing left attached; spacer variant; fence reversal variant; squareness from keys plus parallel perpendicular bores; hand-held, unpowered) each rest on an exact affirmative passage. Antecedent basis and dependency order were checked and are sound; the "fixed fence" definition is lexicography for the disclosure's own word "fixed."

Numerals: all 27 ledger entries (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94) were checked for one-part-one-meaning, appear at least once in a figure brief, and every numeral used in a brief or in the description appears in the ledger with the same label; parenthetical figure cross-references in the description (14/FIG. 4, 12/FIG. 3, 16 and 18/FIG. 2, 52/FIG. 5, 72/FIG. 3, 54/FIG. 5, 74/FIG. 3, 58/FIGS. 1 and 5, 78/FIGS. 1 and 3, 60/FIG. 5, 80/FIG. 3, 40/FIG. 4, 26 and 94/FIG. 7, 34 and 36/FIG. 6) all resolve to figures that list those numerals.

Figures: all seven briefs were checked against the disclosure. The generic outlines that had to be chosen (plain block carriages, plain round knobs, plain rectangular fence body, schematic slot and notch, page placement such as the fence at the left) are labeled "shown schematically," the claims and description stay shape-neutral, and no proportion, count, material, taper, angle, depth, runout, or contact topology beyond the source is verbalized; no "by way of example," "any closed outline," or similar shape-justifying sentence appears in the application text or Brief Description. Substantive relationships that are stated (portion 32 on the rail side facing the edge and contacting it; spacer plate faces against portion 32 and edge 92; key into slot; shoe below rail; bore through carriage registering with slot; pointers ending beside the marks; index at midpoint and V-notch in the second end) each trace to an affirmative passage. Section lines carry the same designation in all three places: line 3-3 in the FIG. 2 brief, the FIG. 3 brief title, and the Brief Description; line 5-5 likewise, with the stepped offset legs and arrow direction consistent between FIG. 2, FIG. 3, FIG. 5, and the elevation direction of FIG. 4.

Text hygiene: claims and description use identical relationships and terms ("registers with," "downwardly projecting portion," "mounting holes," "clamping shoe," "transverse center index"), the Brief Description matches each brief's view type and subject, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains. Background prior-art characterizations were left for the later citation review. No untraced technical assertion and no internal inconsistency was found.

input.summary: Preflight source-fidelity review of the full candidate (title through abstract, numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs) against input/disclosure.md and the USER passage in input/conversation.md, with input/brief.md used only for formalities. I built a complete ledger and traced every element: rail 10 with flat lower face 14, upper face 12, straight longitudinal slot 16 through the rail, and printed distance marks 18 beside the slot; fixed fence 30 at the first end, perpendicular to the rail, with downwardly projecting portion 32 below the lower face bearing on workpiece edge 92; reversibility by two screws 34 in two corresponding mounting holes 36 moving portion 32 from one longitudinal side to the other while the marked upper face still faces the user; removable spacer plate 40 with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing hole separation; two separate guide carriages 50/70 with keys 52/72 in the slot that block rotation while permitting sliding, cylindrical drill bushings 54/74 whose bores pass completely through the carriage and register with the slot, bores parallel to one another and perpendicular to the flat lower face; threaded clamp knobs 58/78 above the rail with shanks passing through carriage and slot into clamping shoes 60/80 below the rail that clamp the rail when tightened and free it when loosened; pointers 62/82 aligned with their bore axes and read against the distance marks so their difference is the center-to-center spacing; transverse center index 24 at the midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch 26 in the second end aligned with the index and with pencil centerline 94; the full setting, placing, aligning, drilling, and lift-away method; materials (rigid polymer or metal for rail, fence, carriage bodies, shoes, spacer plate, pointers, knobs; hardened metal for the replaceable bushings); and the negative recitation of no motor, battery, electronic sensor, or network connection. Each of the 22 claims (independents 1, 13, 18 and dependents 2-12, 14-17, 19-22) was traced limitation by limitation to an affirmative disclosure passage, including the reversibility, same-reading-direction, spacer-plate setback, hardened/replaceable bushing, materials, hand-operated, and perpendicular-drilling limitations; no limitation rests on drafter prose, prior art, or common engineering knowledge. Claim terms and description terms match (rail, fixed fence, guide carriage, drill bushing, clamp knob, clamping shoe, spacer plate, pointer, transverse center index, sight notch, downwardly projecting portion), the brief's preserved terminology is used, and no means-plus-function form appears. All 26 numerals in draft/numerals.md are used consistently, each denotes exactly one part, every numeral cited in the description appears in the ledger and in at least one figure list, and no figure list contains an unledgered numeral. Section lines carry the same repeated designation everywhere: line 3-3 in the FIG. 2 brief, in the FIG. 3 title, and in the Brief Description (section through second guide carriage 70), and line 5-5 likewise (section through first guide carriage 50); the stepped offset planes are a sectioning convention forced by the bore and knob shank both passing through the same longitudinal slot. Figure geometry was checked for undisclosed functional-surface substance: schematic blocks, round knob bodies, plain rectangular fence outlines, break line, and slot outline are confined to the figure briefs, add no depth, taper, angle, runout, or contact topology beyond the source, and the application text and Brief Description contain no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language justifying a renderer's choice. The sight notch is described only as shallow and V-shaped in the second end aligned with the center index, exactly as disclosed. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, or unresolved alternative remains, and the Background's prior-art characterizations were left for the separate citation trace. No untraced technical assertion or verified internal inconsistency was found.
